title: 🏳️‍🌈 Rainbow Flag Emoji Meaning: Pride and Identity
description: The rainbow flag emoji 🏳️‍🌈 stands for LGBTQ+ pride, identity and support. Learn what it signals in bios and messages, its history, and how it differs from 🌈.
summary: The rainbow flag emoji 🏳️‍🌈 represents LGBTQ+ pride. People use it to say they are gay, lesbian, bisexual, transgender, or queer, to show support as allies, to mark Pride events, and to label spaces and content as LGBTQ+ friendly. It depicts the six-stripe Pride flag.
meaning: 🏳️‍🌈 is one of the few emojis whose main meaning is an identity. In a bio or display name it most often says the account holder is part of the LGBTQ+ community. In a message it can accompany coming out, celebrate a wedding or anniversary, cheer a friend on, or tag plans for a Pride parade. Businesses, venues, and creators use it to signal that queer people are welcome.

The flag it shows dates to 1978, when artist Gilbert Baker designed a rainbow banner for San Francisco's Gay Freedom Day celebrations. His first version had eight stripes; the familiar six-stripe flag of red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and violet soon became standard. Baker assigned each color a meaning, such as red for life and violet for spirit. The emoji arrived in 2016, giving a symbol already flown worldwide a place on the keyboard.

Use by allies is common and generally welcomed, especially in June, when Pride Month fills feeds with rainbow flags. That breadth means the emoji alone does not tell you someone's orientation: a parent, a teacher, or a brand may be expressing support. Within the community it is also used playfully, as in “that outfit is very 🏳️‍🌈.” Newer designs such as the Progress Pride flag have no emoji of their own, so 🏳️‍🌈 serves as the general-purpose symbol.

contexts.label: In bios and profiles
contexts.body: A 🏳️‍🌈 in a profile usually signals identity or firm allyship, and many people place it beside pronouns or other pride emojis such as the transgender flag. On dating apps it helps users find each other quickly. Since it can mean either “I am” or “I support,” it is worth not assuming which without other cues.

contexts.label: During Pride Month
contexts.body: Each June the flag spreads far beyond personal accounts. Parade photos, event listings, corporate logos, and sports teams all adopt it. That saturation draws some criticism from within the community when companies use the flag for a month without backing it up, a practice often called rainbow washing.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Between friends, 🏳️‍🌈 can be a celebration (“she said yes 🏳️‍🌈💍”), a quiet signal of safety to someone who has just come out, or a joke about something being flamboyantly gay. Tone depends on who is speaking; affectionate in-group humor can read as mockery when it comes from outside.

examples.text: Told my parents last night. It went better than I hoped 🏳️‍🌈
examples.meaning: The sender is sharing that they came out to their family.

examples.text: Pride is the 14th this year, who's marching with me? 🏳️‍🌈🎉
examples.meaning: An invitation to attend a Pride parade together.

examples.text: Happy anniversary to my wife, ten years 🏳️‍🌈❤️
This bar is 🏳️‍🌈 friendly btw, you'll love it
examples.meaning: Reassuring a friend that a venue is welcoming to LGBTQ+ people.
A parent expressing support for an LGBTQ+ child.

combos.meaning: Pride that explicitly includes transgender people; common in bios and event posts.
Love and support for the LGBTQ+ community or for a same-sex couple.
Celebratory, playful queerness; often captions outfits, parties, or coming-out posts.

confusedWith.difference: 🌈 is the weather phenomenon: an arc, with no flag. It is used for hope, luck, and colorful things in general, and sometimes for Pride, but it does not carry the specific identity meaning the flag does.
🏳️‍⚧️ has light blue, pink, and white stripes and represents transgender people specifically. The rainbow flag covers the wider LGBTQ+ community; many people display both.
🏳️ is the technical base of the rainbow flag and may appear beside 🌈 on old software. Alone it means surrender, which has nothing to do with Pride.

avoid: Do not use it to mock someone or to speculate about a person's orientation; outing or teasing with the flag is hurtful.
Avoid adding it to marketing unless the support behind it is real, since audiences are quick to call out empty rainbow branding.
Remember that in some countries displaying LGBTQ+ symbols carries legal or social risk, so do not tag others with it without their consent.
design: All major platforms draw a waving flag with six horizontal stripes: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple, top to bottom. Styles differ slightly in how much the flag ripples and in the pole. The emoji is a sequence that joins the white flag to the rainbow; systems too old to support it show those two emojis side by side instead of one flag.

faqs.q: What does 🏳️‍🌈 mean in a bio?
faqs.a: Most often that the person is LGBTQ+, and sometimes that they are a committed ally. It works as a quick way to state identity and to signal that the account is a friendly space.

faqs.q: Can straight people use the rainbow flag emoji?
faqs.a: Yes. Allies use it to show support, especially around Pride or when congratulating LGBTQ+ friends. The usual courtesy is to use it sincerely, not as a joke at someone's expense or as decoration for marketing.

faqs.q: Why does my rainbow flag show as a white flag and a rainbow?
faqs.a: The emoji is stored as two characters linked by an invisible joiner. If your device, app, or font predates support for that link, it draws each part separately. A software update normally restores the single flag.

faqs.q: When did the rainbow flag emoji come out?
faqs.a: It was introduced in 2016 and appeared on iPhones and other major platforms soon afterward. Before then, people typically used the plain rainbow 🌈 to stand in for the Pride flag.

faqs.q: Is there a Progress Pride flag emoji?
faqs.a: No. Variants such as the Progress Pride flag and flags for bisexual, lesbian, or nonbinary identities are not in the emoji set. The six-stripe rainbow flag and the transgender flag are the only pride flags with their own emojis.
